title: ALMA hints at the presence of turbulent disk galaxies at z > 5
question: Determine whether galaxies in the first billion years of the Universe have already formed a dynamically cold rotating disk similar to their local counterparts.

what.value: Stellar masses, SFRs, and dust masses of the target sample collected from the literature

evidence.quote: The values of stellar mass, SFR, and dust mass were obtained from the literature (see Table \[\[tab:properties\]\](#tab:properties) for details).
Table \[\[tab:properties\]\](#tab:properties) lists the properties collected from the literature of the galaxies analyzed in this work.

evidence.loc: Velocity dispersion and $V_{\rm max}/\sigma_{\rm gas}$ evolution with redshift
evidence.quote: While our $V_{\rm max}/\sigma_{\rm gas}$ ratios agreet with the estimates found for galaxies in the ALPINE survey (cite: Jones:2021), our analysis differs from the results determined in the sample of galaxies studied by (cite: Sharda:2019),(cite: Rizzo:2020), (cite: Rizzo:2021), (cite: Fraternali:2021) and (cite: Lelli:2021), hereafter the dusty star-forming galaxy (DSFG) sample (blue box at $4<z<5$).
The values of $M_{\rm dust}$ were obtained from (cite: Pozzi:2021) and (cite: Bethermin:2020) for the ALPINE sample, and from (cite: Aravena:2016) for the DSFG.

recipe.goal: Generate moment maps and apply S/N masking
recipe.method: Pixel-by-pixel Gaussian fitting on the datacube plus a constant for continuum residual to derive zeroth, first, and second moment maps, then mask pixels below S/N thresholds.
key_parameters: 5 sigma_flux threshold for [C II]; 3 sigma_flux threshold for [O III]; vmin and vmax at 16th and 84th percentiles of best-fitting Gaussian

recipe.method: Generate 3D mock datacubes using KINMS with 5x10^5 line-emitting particles for an exponential disk (and optional Sérsic bulge for M* > 10^10 M_sun), convolved with the ALMA PSF.
key_parameters: 5x10^5 particles; R0 = 5 kpc for disk mass M_d; Sérsic index n = 4 for bulge
assumptions: Thin exponential disk with constant mass-to-light ratio; negligible dark matter contribution within two scale radii; for disk+bulge model, bulge effective radius r_e = 0.5 r_d and bulge mass M_b = M_* from literature.

recipe.goal: Method I: 2D kinematic fitting of resolved galaxies
recipe.method: Three-step MCMC fitting of moment maps using EMCEE: (1) fit flux map for center (x0, y0) and scale radius (r_d) and fix them; (2) fit velocity map for v_sys, inc, PA, and M_rot; (3) fit all three moment maps simultaneously using step 2 results as priors, sampling uncorrelated pixels separated by more than the beam semi-major axis across 100 trials.
key_parameters: 100 random pixel-extraction trials; 50% burn-in phase; median and 16th/84th percentiles for parameters and errors
assumptions: Pixels separated by a distance greater than the semi-major axis of the beam are uncorrelated.

recipe.goal: Method II: 1D kinematic fitting of spatially integrated spectra for unresolved galaxies
recipe.method: Fit the flux map to get scale radius r_d and initial inclination constraint; fix M_rot = M_* + M_gas (using alpha_[CII] = 30 M_sun/L_sun); fit spatially integrated spectrum with KINMS model spectrum using MCMC, then divide derived sigma_gas by empirical correction factor of 1.6.
key_parameters: alpha_[CII] = 30 M_sun/L_sun; correction factor = 1.6 on sigma_gas; flat prior on sigma_gas in [0, 300] km s^-1; flat prior on inc within +/- 3 sigma of flux-map fit
assumptions: M_rot = M_* + M_gas; alpha_[CII] = 30 M_sun/L_sun with 0.2 dex uncertainty.

answer_key.quantity: Median gas velocity dispersion at z > 5 (Method I)

evidence.quote: The values of the velocity dispersion obtained for galaxies at $z>5$ that were studied with method I range between 37 ${\rm km~s^{-1}}$and 132 ${\rm km~s^{-1}}$, with a median velocity dispersion of $67^{+15}_{-13}$ ${\rm km~s^{-1}}$.

answer_key.quantity: Median V_max / sigma_gas at z > 5 (Method I)

evidence.quote: For the rotational support, we find a median value of $V_{\rm max}/\sigma_{\rm gas} = 2$ that is compatible with turbulent but still rotationally supported disk galaxies.

answer_key.quantity: Median gas velocity dispersion (Method II, corrected)

evidence.quote: Galaxies analyzed with method II show a velocity dispersion, corrected by a factor 1.6 (see Sec. [3.6](#sec:method2)), between 37 and 126 km s$^{-1}$ and a median value of $60^{+19}_{-11}$ ${\rm km~s^{-1}}$, which is compatible with the median value obtained with the other method.
The median value of $V_{\rm max}/\sigma_{\rm gas}$ is 3.2, which is slightly higher than the result found with method I.

score_reason: All ALMA project codes are listed and public, software packages (CASA, KINMS, EMCEE) and equations are well specified, and full per-target results are tabulated, though custom fitting scripts and exact per-target tclean/aperture settings are not released.
rediscovery_reason: Uses public archival ALMA data with explicit project codes, standard public tools (CASA, KINMS, EMCEE), a clearly described 3-step fitting methodology, and complete per-galaxy numerical results in Table 1.
